title: The Interview - CBSE Official Practice DPP

questions.question:
[Extract Context: "Maybe I give the impression of doing many things. But i n the end, I am 
convinced I am always doing the same thing… And then I have a secret. Did 
you know what will happen i f you eliminate the e mpty spaces from the 
universe, eliminate the empty ..."]

Read the questions given below. Imagine they were interjections raised by 
the interviewer based on the above extr act. Choose the option that correctly 
describes the given questions. 

(i) If you are “alway s doing the same thing”, isn’t your work lackin g in 
originality? 
(ii) Could you elaborate on these larger ethical, philosophical int erests that 
inform your work? 
(iii) All writing happens in empty spaces. In fact, why don’t I tell you all about 
my experiences?
options: (i) is not relevant; (ii) is appropriate; and (iii) is unnecessary
(i) is appropriate; (ii) is repetitive; and (iii) is useful information
(i) is inappropriate; (ii) is relevant; and (iii) is not relevant
(i) is unnecessary; (ii) is intrusive; and (iii) is extrapolatory
questions.explanation: CBSE Official Question Bank Answer Key: Option (C).

questions.question:
According to Christopher Silvester, the interview can be “i n its highest form, 
a source of truth”. Choose the option that does NOT enable this?
options:
An interview allows for discovery of new knowledge about the interviewee 
and/ or the subject being discussed.

An inter view enables the interviewer to probe deeply, seek clarifications, 
and confirm understandings.

An interview represents an opportunity to open doors to experiences that 
may not otherwise find a voice.

An interview requires the int erviewer to have in -depth prior knowledge of 
the interviewee and the subject.
questions.explanation: CBSE Official Question Bank Stand-Alone Answer Key: Option (D).

questions.question:
Column A below describes Rudyard Kipling’s vi ews on interviews. Column 
B provides fictional descriptions of some of K ipling’s works if they were 
about interviews and interviewers. Choose the option that correctly matches 
interview attributes given in Column A to the works in Column B: 

Column A Column B 

1. immoral (i) ‘The Mark of the Beast’ – An illicit tale of 
unforgivable offences against man and 
society. 

2. cowardly (ii) ‘The Jungle Boo k’ – A jou rney into the 
corrupt jungle of information where conscience 
and principles do not exist. 

3. vile (iii) ‘The Light that Failed’ – A story of 
audacious truth being left i n the dark alleys of 
craven scandal and misrepresentation. 

4. criminal (iv) ‘The Man Who Would be King’ – A saga of 
evil depravity of a man who ruled over heroes 
and became a villain.
questions.explanation: CBSE Official Question Bank Stand-Alone Answer Key: Option (B).

questions.question:
Mukund Padmanabhan mentions that much like his novels, Umberto Eco’s 
“scholarly work has a cer tain playful and personal quality about it.” To what 
is this attributed?
options: Eco thought regular academic style was depersonalised, dry and boring.
Eco presented his first Doctoral dissertation in Italy in this style.
Eco realized that scholarly books should tell the story of the research.
Eco identified himself with the academic and scholarly community.
questions.explanation: CBSE Official Question Bank Stand-Alone Answer Key: Option (C).

questions.question:
Umberto Eco mentioned that he was not puz zled by the trem endous mass 
popularity of his novel, The Name of the Rose. What does this tell you about 
Umberto Eco?
options:
He believes he understands re adership trends well, and writes 
accordingly to ensure mass appeal.

He elevates himself above publishe rs and journalists who were surprised 
by the success of the book.

He respects and understands that there are variations in people’s reading 
choices and experiences.

He feels tha t the success of a bo ok is a mystery, and there was no point 
pondering over it.
questions.explanation: CBSE Official Question Bank Stand-Alone Answer Key: Option (C).
